notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 15 this time, because my research tools stopped working before I read a single page.

My first attempt tried to open eight commentary pages at once and hit the tool's usage limit. When I tried again with just one page (Enduring Word on Isaiah 15), I was told I had no tool calls left for this turn. So no pages loaded.

Your rules say to report only what the sources actually say, with a URL for every point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. With nothing read, any verse notes would break those rules, so I haven't written any.

If you ask again, I'll go through these pages one at a time:
- **Verse-by-verse commentary:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-15/ and preceptaustin.org's Isaiah 15 page
- **Older commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit):** biblehub.com/commentaries/isaiah/15-1.htm through 15-9.htm
- **Wesley's Notes:** studylight.org
- **Modern scholarship:** netbible.org's notes on Isaiah 15
- **Catholic:** newadvent.org (Haydock and the Church Fathers)
- **Differences between traditions and popular modern teaching:** searches on the other approved sites

Then I'll write the notes verse by verse ("v. 1: …") with a URL for each point, and leave out anything I can't find. Isaiah 15 is mostly about places and mourning, so the "differences between traditions" and "popular modern teaching" sections may end up short or empty. If so, I'll say that rather than make up disagreements.
